scope: Local source, configuration, unit, authenticated loopback Redis 8.2.8, real BullMQ, and loopback OTLP/HTTP protobuf evidence for bounded durable-queue backlog telemetry. No production, staging, provider sandbox, external collector, customer data, or source-system write was used.

priorEvidence.purpose: The immediately preceding 44-migration, 446-test observability and durable-trace baseline.

metricTemporality.reason: The pinned cumulative last-value aggregation retains a prior observable-gauge point after its callback stops observing. Explicit worker delta collection lets a follower or failed former leader stop exporting that queue series.

boundedReadContract.readyAgeDefinition: Maximum age since job creation among the next dispatchable waiting, paused, and prioritized list heads.
boundedReadContract.reasonExactPriorityOldestRejected: BullMQ orders prioritized jobs by priority rather than creation time, so an exact creation-age scan would grow with backlog.

singleWriterContract.leaseToken: random per process, compare-renewed and compare-deleted

failureIsolation.shutdownOrder: monitor, monitor BullMQ client, dedicated monitor Redis, then existing worker resources and OTLP shutdown

focusedVerification.command: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test

authenticatedRedisAndOtlpVerification.command: REDIS_URL=<authenticated-loopback-url> pnpm exec vitest run --project integration apps/worker/src/queue-observability.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

rejectedIntermediateDesign.design: Cumulative observable gauge with only a process-local lease-expiring snapshot
rejectedIntermediateDesign.testResult: A forced export after follower transition still contained the prior queue gauge because the pinned SDK cumulative temporal processor merged the last observation.
rejectedIntermediateDesign.correction: The worker exporter now selects delta temporality explicitly, and the same post-follower assertion passes.

limitations: The lease and three clients ran on one workstation against one standalone Redis process, not independently scheduled worker hosts, Sentinel, Cluster, or a managed Redis topology.
The local Redis server used authenticated loopback TCP without TLS or an ACL user split. This is not production network, identity, transport, failover, or capacity evidence.

The test exercised one lease owner, one follower, exact fixed BullMQ states, and one ownership transition. It did not exercise process crash during polling, Redis partition/restart, clock skew, sustained backlog, replica churn, or multi-host lease fairness.
Ready-head maximum age is intentionally not the exact oldest creation age across all prioritized jobs. It observes only the next dispatchable head of each bounded ready list.

The OTLP receiver captured real protobuf locally. No protected collector/backend, TLS/authentication, egress allowlist, access/retention policy, dashboard aggregation, threshold, silence rule, alert delivery, acknowledgement, or on-call response was exercised.

Worker delta and API cumulative temporality are explicit and standard OTLP forms, but compatibility with the selected production collector/backend and its dashboard queries still requires staging verification.
Connector freshness, webhook verification, normalization failure, review age, AI, and representative business/SLO signals remain separate work.

Queue monitoring is deliberately lossy and non-authoritative. Missing samples require a silence alert and cannot authorize queue mutation, financial action, retry, approval, or source-system state change.
claim: ReconAI now has a locally verified, constant-size, low-cardinality durable-queue state and ready-frontier monitor with Redis single-writer ownership, bounded failure isolation, and no stale gauge after a follower transition. This is local component evidence, not staging or production readiness, an SLO, a capacity result, or an exercised operational alert.
